note: Names, descriptions and grades are the official PlayStation 5 list. The guide on each trophy is our own advice built from its official description, not yet checked in the game; where the description does not pin a place down, the guide says so.

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: The platinum pops the moment the other 54 trophies are yours, so there is no separate task here — it is the sum of everything in this guide. Play the story first, then work the roadmap in order: story and stranger strands, then the open-world checklists (exploration, vehicles, activities), then the grinds (stunts, challenges, money). Keep this tracker open as you play and tick trophies off as they pop; the Next up planner will always point at the nearest ones. Expect 60 to 80 hours for a first platinum run, longer if you stop to enjoy Leonida.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade). Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: Gone Fishing is the opening mission, so this is the first trophy most players will earn. Follow the on-screen prompts through the introduction: it teaches movement, driving and the basic controls, and the trophy pops on the mission-complete screen. Nothing can be missed here — the mission is unskippable and always available from the start. If you are new to the series, take your time with the driving tutorial; the handling you learn here carries through the whole game.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade). Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Finish every story mission in Chapter 1. The chapter is linear — play the missions in the order they appear on the map and the trophy pops after the chapter's final cutscene. There is no way to miss this: chapters cannot be skipped, and any mission can be replayed from the pause menu if you fail it. A good habit from the start: save often, and do the side activities the game introduces as you meet them instead of leaving them all for the end.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade). Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Finish every story mission in Chapter 2. The missions get longer here and the wanted system starts to bite: keep a fast car nearby for getaways, and use your partner when a mission lets you switch characters — the second character often has the better angle. As with Chapter 1, nothing here is missable; the trophy pops after the chapter's closing mission. This is a good chapter to start the collectibles in earnest, since you will be driving across most of Leonida anyway.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade). Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Finish every story mission in Chapter 3. By now the map is fully open, so the missions spread across Vice City and the wider state — use fast travel where the game offers it and keep your weapons stocked before each mission, because the combat missions in this chapter are the toughest so far. The trophy pops after the chapter finale. If a mission keeps beating you, drop the difficulty in the settings or replay it with a better loadout; mission replays do not cost you the trophy.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade). Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Finish every story mission in Chapter 4. This is the longest and hardest chapter: missions run long, checkpoints are sparse, and the finale chains several objectives together. Go in with full health, armor and ammo, and use cover — the game's combat rewards patience over rushing. The trophy pops after the chapter's final mission, which sets up the finale. Once it pops, you are one chapter from the end of the story; before starting the finale, clear any stranger strands you have open, since some of them are easier with the full map and full arsenal.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade). Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: Finish the final story mission. This is the gold trophy for completing the story, and it is the one story trophy we flag as possibly missable: if the story branches near the end, the final mission may differ by the path you take, so save in a separate slot before the point of no return (the game warns you when it arrives) and keep that save until the trophy pops. The finale is long — expect an hour or two of chained objectives — so go in fully stocked and save at every checkpoint the game offers. The trophy pops on the mission-complete screen, and the credits roll after it.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade). Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Breakfast Run is a story mission — play it when its marker appears on the map and finish it to pop the trophy. The name suggests an early-morning job, likely a delivery or pickup run with your partner, so expect driving under time pressure and a tail to lose. Story missions can be replayed, so there is nothing to miss: if you fail, retry from the checkpoint. The exact route is not pinned down in the official description, so follow the in-game GPS and the mission's own instructions.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade). Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: The Cartel Heist is a story heist mission — play it when its marker appears and finish it. Heists in this series are multi-stage: a setup phase, then the job itself, then the getaway. Stock up on ammo and armor before you start, use your partner to cover angles you cannot, and expect a long police chase on the way out — a fast, durable car beats a flashy one for the escape. The trophy pops on completion and the mission is replayable, so it cannot be missed.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade). Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Child's Play is a story mission — play it when its marker appears and finish it. The title points to a mission involving family, so expect a character-driven job rather than a pure shootout: listen to the dialogue, follow the markers, and do not rush the scripted beats. As with every story mission, it can be replayed from the pause menu, so the trophy cannot be missed. The exact location is not pinned down in the official description — follow the map marker when it shows up.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade). Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Headliners is a story mission — play it when its marker appears and finish it. The name suggests a music or nightlife job, likely set around a club or venue in Vice City, so expect a mix of driving, on-foot sections and a set-piece moment. Story missions are replayable, so the trophy cannot be missed. If the mission has a stealth or timing section, take it slow on the first attempt and learn the pattern before pushing for speed.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade). Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: VCIA Takedown is a story mission at Vice City International Airport — play it when its marker appears and finish it. Expect a heavy combat section on airport grounds and a vehicle-based escape; the airport is wide open, so use cover and keep moving between the terminals and the tarmac. Bring a rifle and plenty of ammo, and grab a fast car before the getaway leg starts. The mission is replayable, so the trophy cannot be missed.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade). Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Operation Savage Glory is a story mission — play it when its marker appears and finish it. The military-style name points to a large-scale operation with heavy weapons and vehicles, so expect the toughest combat of the early story: armor up, keep a powerful weapon ready, and use your partner to flank. The mission is replayable, so the trophy cannot be missed. The exact location is not pinned down in the official description — follow the map marker.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade). Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: Reach 100% completion in the in-game stats. This is the second gold trophy and the real grind of the platinum: 100% counts the story, the stranger strands, the collectibles, the activities and the checklists the game tracks in its stats page. Open the stats early and use it as your to-do list — it shows exactly what counts and what is left. The biggest chunks are usually the collectibles and the activity completions, so do those alongside the story instead of leaving them all for the end. Nothing here is missable in the usual sense: everything that counts toward 100% can be done after the story, in free roam. When the stats hit 100%, the trophy pops.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade). Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Pull off 250 stunts — jumps, near misses, drifts, airtime and the like. The counter is cumulative across the whole game, so every jump you hit while driving around counts; by the end of the story you will already have a good chunk of them. To finish the count quickly, find a stunt jump or a ramp you can loop, and chain airtime with near misses on a busy highway: jump, land clean, and immediately thread traffic for near-miss bonuses. The PSN count is 250, so check your stats page to see where you stand. Nothing is missable — stunts can be done any time in free roam.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade); PSNProfiles for PSN's count of 250. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try each of the 9 activity types once. The game introduces activities as you explore — racing, fishing, the shooting range, drone races, arcade games, bowling, meditation, hunting and one more the official description counts as the ninth. You do not need to win or finish any of them; starting one of each type is enough for the trophy to pop. Open the activities menu on the map to see which types you have not tried yet, then visit one of each. Nothing is missable — every activity stays available in free roam.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade); PSNProfiles for PSN's count of 9 activity types. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in all 42 Shooting Range challenges. There are 42 challenges across the range's disciplines — pistols, rifles, shotguns and the rest — and each needs a gold score. Learn the scoring first: accuracy beats speed on most lanes, and the gold threshold is shown before you start, so you know exactly what to beat. Start with the weapon types you are best with, then grind the hard ones in short sessions instead of all at once. Use the range's practice mode to learn each lane's target pattern before going for gold. Nothing is missable — the range is open in free roam and challenges can be retried without limit.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade); PSNProfiles for PSN's count of 42 challenges. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at all 14 locations. Drone races are short checkpoint races flown from a first-person drone view — the trick is cutting corners through the rings instead of flying the racing line, and using the boost on the straights. Each location is a separate race, so you need 14 wins in total; the map marks every Top Fun location once you have found it. If a location keeps beating you, retry it immediately — there is no penalty for failing, and the race restarts in seconds. Nothing is missable.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade); PSNProfiles for PSN's count of 14 locations. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races. Races are scattered across Leonida — street races, off-road, boat and air races all count, as long as each one is a different race. Pick the vehicle the race suggests, learn the route on a first slow run if you need to, and use slipstreaming on the straights. You do not need to win every race type, just 20 distinct ones, so skip the ones you hate and do the ones you enjoy twice over different routes. The race markers stay on the map in free roam, so nothing is missable.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade). Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Cal is a fishing rival you meet through the fishing activity — challenge him at a fishing spot and out-fish him. Fishing in this game is a timing mini-game: wait for the bite, hook at the right moment, then reel with steady tension and let the line slacken when the fish runs, or it snaps. Buy the better rod and bait from a tackle shop first if you are struggling; the upgrade makes the challenge noticeably easier. The challenge can be retried, so nothing is missable. The exact fishing spots are not pinned down in the official description — look for the fishing markers on the map.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade). Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Complete one arcade game. Arcades are found in Vice City — walk up to a cabinet, start a game, and play it through to the end. You do not need a high score or a win, just a completed game, so pick the shortest cabinet you can find and finish it. The trophy pops when the game ends. Nothing is missable — the arcades are open in free roam.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade). Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Andy's stranger strand. Stranger strands are side-mission chains given by characters you meet around Leonida — Andy's chain ends with this mission. Play through all of Andy's missions in order (they appear as markers on the map once the strand starts) and the trophy pops after the last one. Stranger strands stay available in free roam after the story, so nothing is missable. The exact locations are not pinned down in the official description — follow the strand's map markers.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade). Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Kenton's stranger strand. Play through Kenton's missions in order until the strand ends — the trophy pops after the final one. The title hints at a boat, so expect at least one mission on the water; keep a fast boat in mind for the getaway. Stranger strands stay available after the story, so nothing is missable. Follow the strand's map markers; the exact locations are not pinned down in the official description.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade). Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Billy's stranger strand. Play through Billy's missions in order until the strand ends — the trophy pops after the last one. The title points to a lone-rider theme, likely a bike job, so a fast motorcycle is the right tool for the final mission. Stranger strands stay available after the story, so nothing is missable. Follow the strand's map markers.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade). Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 full stranger mission strands across Leonida. Strangers are the side characters marked on the map — each one has a chain of missions, and finishing all of a chain counts as one strand. There are more than 8 strands in the game, so pick the ones you enjoy and finish 8 of them; the trophy pops on the eighth. The individual final-mission trophies (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone) each count toward this total. Strands stay available in free roam after the story, so nothing is missable — just keep working through the map markers.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade). Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Randy's stranger strand. Play through Randy's missions in order until the strand ends — the trophy pops after the last one. The title points to a supply job, so expect a pickup-and-deliver chain with a tail to lose on the final leg. Stranger strands stay available after the story, so nothing is missable. Follow the strand's map markers.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade). Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Tyrone's stranger strand. Play through Tyrone's missions in order until the strand ends — the trophy pops after the last one. The title suggests a music or DJ angle, so expect a club or venue setting for the finale. Stranger strands stay available after the story, so nothing is missable. Follow the strand's map markers.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade). Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at all 18 meditation spots across Leonida. Meditation spots are quiet scenic points — beaches, hilltops, parks — marked on the map once discovered. At each spot, start the meditation activity and let it run to completion; the counter ticks up per spot, not per session, so each spot only needs one visit. Work through them region by region to avoid backtracking, and use a fast car or a helicopter for the far ones. The PSN count is 18 spots. Nothing is missable — the spots are always there in free roam.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade); PSNProfiles for PSN's count of 18 spots. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt a unique animal for Bret. Bret is a hunting contact — meet him, take the hunt, and track the unique animal he names. Hunting here is a tracking job: follow the trail, stay downwind, and take the shot when the animal is still. Bring a scoped rifle and be patient; spooking the animal means a long walk back to pick up the trail. The trophy pops when the animal is down and the hunt is turned in. The hunt can be retried, so nothing is missable. The exact animal and location are not pinned down in the official description — Bret's mission marker will show the way.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade). Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Complete 3 collectible card sets. Cards are hidden around Leonida — in shops, on benches, in glove boxes — and each set is a themed group of cards. You need three full sets, not every card in the game, so focus on the sets whose cards cluster near each other and finish those first. Cards you have found are marked in the collection menu, so you can see which sets are closest to complete. Nothing is missable — cards stay where they are in free roam and can be picked up any time.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade). Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: Use the WAiNK It feature at 100 locations. WAiNK It is the game's photo or check-in action at scenic spots — open it at a marked location and the counter ticks up. The spots are spread across the whole state, so the fastest route is to sweep region by region with a fast vehicle, hitting every marker you pass. The map marks locations you have already done, so you will not repeat one by accident. The PSN count is 100. Nothing is missable — the locations are always there.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade); PSNProfiles for PSN's count of 100 locations. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Complete 50 challenges. Challenges are the game's open-world task list — stunt jumps, near misses, headshots, getaways and the like — and the counter is cumulative, so you will have completed many of them just by playing. Open the challenges menu to see which ones are closest to done, then target those: the easy ones (a set number of near misses, a set number of headshots) fall quickly in free roam. Nothing is missable — challenges can be completed any time after the story.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade). Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: Lose a 4-star wanted level while your partner is with you, then escape. Get your partner in the car, commit a crime big enough to reach 4 stars (rob a store, or take on the police in a busy area), then break line of sight and hide until the stars clear — a parking garage or a tunnel works, and switching cars mid-chase helps. The trophy pops once the wanted level is fully gone with your partner still with you. It can be retried as often as you like, so nothing is missable. Do it in free roam, not during a mission, so a failure costs you nothing.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade). Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your wanted level. The trick is the order: rob the first shop, keep the wanted level alive (do not hide long enough for it to clear), drive straight to the second, then the third. Pick three shops close together on one street so the drive between them is seconds, not minutes, and keep your partner in the car the whole time. If the wanted level clears, the chain resets and you start over — no harm done, just try again. Do it in free roam so a failure costs nothing.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade). Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Discover 100 vehicles. Every distinct vehicle you get into counts toward the total — cars, bikes, boats, aircraft — so the fastest way is variety: drive everything you see, and visit the places vehicles cluster (dealerships, docks, the airport, car parks). The vehicle menu shows which ones you have discovered, so you can see what is left. The PSN count is 100 distinct vehicles. Nothing is missable — vehicles are everywhere in free roam, and story missions alone will hand you a good share of the total.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade); PSNProfiles for PSN's count of 100 vehicles. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus. Combat Focus is the game's slow-motion aiming mode — trigger it when a group of enemies is in front of you, then pick them off one by one while time crawls. The easiest spot is a mission or a gang hideout where enemies cluster: wait until five are in view, trigger Focus, and land five clean hits before the meter runs out. Headshots count the same as body shots, so aim for the biggest target first. It can be retried any time in free roam, so nothing is missable.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade). Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure at Vice City International Airport. This one we flag as possibly missable: the description points to a specific moment at the airport — leaving by a route that is not the scheduled one — and it may only be available during a story beat or a particular airport state. Our advice: the moment you first reach VCIA in the story, look for a way out that is not the main exit — a service road, a runway, a cargo gate — and take it. If the trophy does not pop on the first visit, keep trying in free roam: drive through the airport and leave by any gate that is not the passenger exit. Save before you try, in case the moment is one-time.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade). Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: This one is about Rhinos — the tanks. The description is a joke about how hot it gets inside one, and the trophy most likely pops for getting into a Rhino and using it, or for surviving an encounter with one. Our advice: steal a Rhino from the military base or a mission that spawns one, drive it around, and fire the cannon a few times; if the trophy does not pop on entry, take it into a wanted-level fight and use it there. The exact trigger is not pinned down in the official description, so treat the first Rhino you find as the test: get in, drive, shoot, and see. It can be retried, so nothing is missable.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade). Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected. This is a stealth job: go in quiet, keep your weapon holstered until the moment you need it, and use the back entrance if the store has one. Watch the staff's patrol pattern and the cameras — move when their backs are turned, grab the goods, and leave the same quiet way. If you are spotted, the attempt fails, but you can walk out and try again immediately; the trophy only counts a clean run. Do it in free roam with no mission active, so a failure costs nothing. The exact store is not pinned down in the official description — any jewelry store should work, so pick the quietest one you find.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade). Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape from each one. Bank vaults are the big robberies: each one needs a plan, a crew or your partner, and a getaway. Do them one at a time — crack the vault, grab the cash, then lose the wanted level before the next one. A fast, durable getaway car parked close to the exit makes each escape far easier, and doing the vaults in the quieter parts of the state keeps the police response lighter. The counter is cumulative, so the five do not need to be in a row. Nothing is missable — vaults can be robbed again in free roam.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade). Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape. Armored trucks drive set routes around the city — spot one, block it with your car, and force it to stop, then crack the back and grab the cash before the police arrive. A sticky bomb or a heavy weapon opens the doors fastest; then get in your getaway car and lose the wanted level. The trophy pops once you have escaped clean. It can be retried as often as you like, so nothing is missable. If the truck keeps getting away, chase it on a motorcycle — you can keep up with it and block it at the next intersection.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade). Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Explore all 52 areas of Leonida. The state is divided into 52 named areas, and visiting each one ticks it off — the map shows which areas you have been to, so you can see the gaps. The fastest route is a road trip: take a fast car or a helicopter and sweep the map region by region, touching every area on the way. The PSN count is 52 areas. Nothing is missable — every area is open in free roam, and you will have covered most of them just by playing the story.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade); PSNProfiles for PSN's count of 52 areas. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob an illegal operation belonging to each of the 9 gangs. Gangs run hidden operations around Leonida — drug labs, chop shops, stash houses — and each gang has its own. Find one operation per gang, rob it, and escape; the trophy pops after the ninth gang. The operations are marked once you discover them, so work through the map gang by gang and keep a note of which ones you have done. The PSN count is 9 gangs. Nothing is missable — the operations stay available in free roam.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade); PSNProfiles for PSN's count of 9 gangs. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach. This one we flag as possibly missable: the description points to a specific quiet moment — a cocktail at a beach bar with the ocean in view — and it may only be available at a particular story point or time of day. Our advice: go to Ocean Beach, find the beach bar, order a cocktail and sit through the scene. If nothing pops, try again at sunset or after a story beat — the moment may be tied to the time of day or to a character being with you. Save before you try, in case it is a one-time scene.

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style. Drive into a vehicle showroom, pick a car, and smash straight out through the glass — the classic move. Any showroom works; the trophy pops once you break out through the front. It can be retried any time, so nothing is missable. Do it in free roam and expect a wanted level on the way out — have a getaway car ready, or just enjoy the chase.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade). Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Play a full game at the Kolt & Associates bowling alley. Walk into the alley, start a game, and bowl through all ten frames — the trophy is about the follow-through, so finish the game rather than quitting early. You do not need a high score or a strike; completing the game is enough. The alley is open in free roam, so nothing is missable. Bring your partner along if the alley allows it — some alleys have a two-player lane.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade). Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide: This one is about the partnership — the description is deliberately vague, and the trophy most likely pops for a standout partner moment, such as a high-rated co-op job or a perfect partner rating. Our advice: play the partner missions and jobs, keep your partner alive and involved, and aim for the best outcome on each one; the trophy should pop on the strongest partner performance. The exact trigger is not pinned down in the official description, so if it does not pop after the partner missions, try the partner activities and the co-op robberies — one of them is the trigger. It can be retried, so nothing is missable.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade). Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.guide: Make choices — PSN tracks a count to 500. The game counts the choices you make, big and small, and this trophy pops when the count reaches 500. Every dialogue choice, every fork in a mission, every decision in free roam adds to it, so you will rack up the count naturally by playing the story and saying yes to the optional choices the game offers. We flag it as possibly missable because some choices only appear once: if you rush the story and skip the optional dialogue, the count may stall short of 500, so talk to everyone and take the optional paths when they appear. The count carries across the whole playthrough.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade); PSNProfiles for PSN's count of 500 choices. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.guide: Succeed on a second try. Fail something, then succeed at it on the very next attempt — the trophy pops on the success. The easiest way: pick a short activity you can fail on purpose (a race you quit, a challenge you miss), then do it properly on the next try. It can be done any time in free roam, so nothing is missable. If it does not pop on a mission retry, try it on an activity instead — the trigger counts the second attempt, not the mission itself.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade). Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: Witness something strange. This is the game's weird-event trophy — a UFO, a ghost, a cryptid, something that does not belong. These events are usually tied to a specific place and time: a hilltop at night, a swamp at 3 a.m., a desert road in a storm. Our advice: visit the classic strange spots (the observatory, the deep swamp, the desert) at night and wait a while; the event triggers when you are in the right place at the right time. The exact event is not pinned down in the official description, so this one takes patience — and it can be retried, so nothing is missable.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade). Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Knock someone down with a melee drive-by. Get in a car, pick up speed, and swing a melee weapon out of the window as you pass someone — the trophy pops when the hit lands. A motorcycle makes it easier (no window in the way), and a quiet street with pedestrians gives you a clean target. It can be retried any time in free roam, so nothing is missable. Expect a wanted level after it — that is part of the fun.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade). Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Earn $250,000 by laundering Marked Bills through your contacts. Marked Bills come from the big robberies — bank vaults, armored trucks, heists — and they cannot be spent directly; you launder them through contacts who take a cut and return clean cash. The counter tracks the clean cash you earn this way, so keep robbing and keep laundering: each vault and truck run feeds the total. The PSN count is $250,000 of laundered money. Nothing is missable — robberies and contacts stay available in free roam, so the total just grows as you play.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade); PSNProfiles for PSN's count of $250,000. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops. The counter is cumulative across every shop in the game — clothes, weapons, food, car parts — so it grows naturally as you play and gear up. If you want to finish it faster, spend on the big-ticket items (weapons and car upgrades) rather than snacks, and check the counter in the stats menu to see where you stand. Nothing is missable — shops are always open in free roam, and the money you spend on the story counts toward the total.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade). Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Purchase all 8 garage properties. Garages are bought from the property menu once you have the money — each one gives you storage and a safehouse, and the trophy pops when the eighth is yours. Save up through the story and the robberies first; the garages are expensive, so do not try to buy them all early. The PSN count is 8 garages. Nothing is missable — the properties stay for sale in free roam, and buying them also helps the vehicle collection.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade); PSNProfiles for PSN's count of 8 garage properties. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. The Scooter Bros app is the in-game vehicle service — open it, pick a vehicle you own or have discovered, and register it; each registration ticks the counter up. You need 10 different vehicles, so use the ones you have already discovered across the game rather than buying ten new ones. The counter is cumulative, so registrations from earlier in the game count. Nothing is missable — the app is always available in free roam.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade). Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.
